claim: Alsace has a trio of grand crus permitted to grow non-noble white varieties by exception.
because: Under the cahier des charges, Kaefferkopf may use only Gewurztraminer, Riesling, Pinot Gris and the Muscats, all noble, alone or blended. Its exception is blending, not non-noble grapes. Only Zotzenberg (Sylvaner) and Altenberg de Bergheim (Chasselas and Pinot Blanc as accessory varieties in blends, vines planted before 26 March 2005) admit non-noble whites. Read as written, the stem makes the accepted answer 'kaefferkopf' wrong. The model answer itself treats Kaefferkopf as a blend exception.
fix: Alsace has a trio of grand crus that bend the single-noble-variety rule by exception (Sylvaner, or field blends). Name any one.
